findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a subprocess timeout to the pandoc conversion call (e.g. pypandoc `extra_args` or a wrapper with `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` handling) so a hung pandoc process triggers the existing fallback rather than blocking indefinitely, even if full process hardening is deferred.

The fallback ('return the original Markdown unchanged plus log the fallback once') only triggers on unavailability probe failure or conversion exception — a hung/slow pandoc process that never raises will block indefinitely

findings.finding: The pandoc subprocess has no timeout specified in this story; process hardening is explicitly deferred to a later story (ashy-waterlog-hamadryas), meaning the module ships with a potentially blocking subprocess call and no defense against a hung pandoc process.
findings.location: Implementation section: 'Timeout/process hardening plus GPL/SBOM work belong to ashy-waterlog-hamadryas'

findings.suggested_fix: Pass `timeout=N` (e.g. 10 seconds) to the pypandoc call or wrap it in a `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor` with a timeout. On `TimeoutExpired`, treat it the same as a conversion exception: return original Markdown and log the fallback. The 'full hardening' story can then harden the timeout value rather than add the mechanism from scratch.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the pandoc availability probe and fallback log-once flag are initialized (import-time eager probe, or a threading.Lock / module-level threading.Event guard) so the 'once' guarantee holds under concurrent callers.
evidence: 'Probe availability once' — implies a module-level boolean or sentinel, but no creation point (import time vs. first call) is named.
'log the fallback once' — implies a module-level log-guard flag; no lock, threading.Event, or initialization-at-import guarantee is specified.
The plan targets a remote MCP server deployment shape where concurrent requests are expected.
No RETIRE/cleanup path for these module-level flags is mentioned (minor: they are effectively permanent singletons per process, which is acceptable, but the concurrency gap is not).
findings.finding: The plan introduces module-level shared state for 'log the fallback once' and 'probe availability once' but does not specify the synchronization mechanism. In a multi-threaded server deployment (e.g., a remote MCP server handling concurrent requests), two threads can both read the probe/logged flag as False before either writes True — a classic check-then-act TOCTOU — causing either duplicate pandoc probes or duplicate fallback log emissions. The plan's 'once' guarantee has no defined ownership, initialization point, or atomicity contract.
findings.location: Implementation section: 'Probe availability once. If the binary is unavailable or conversion raises, return the original Markdown unchanged plus log the fallback once.'
scenarios: Remote MCP server with concurrent requests: two threads simultaneously call render_markdown_to_wiki for the first time, both read probe_done=False, both attempt the pandoc probe, both set probe_done=True — redundant subprocess spawning is the minor failure; in the log-once case both emit the fallback log, violating the 'once' contract and potentially flooding structured log aggregators.
CI environment running parallel test workers: if the module is imported fresh per worker the log-once state resets correctly, but if workers share a process the same TOCTOU applies.
findings.suggested_fix: Initialize both the probe result and the log-guard at module import time (eager probe during import) so they are set before any thread can call the function, eliminating the TOCTOU entirely. If lazy probing is preferred, protect the check-then-set with a threading.Lock.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `pypandoc-binary` an optional/extras dependency (e.g. `rebar[dc-wiki]`) or add a platform marker restricting it to supported wheel platforms, so that unsupported platforms (BSD) can still install rebar and rely on the documented runtime fallback rather than failing at pip-resolve time.
evidence: Plan text: 'Pin pypandoc-binary rather than system pypandoc'
pypandoc-binary ships platform-specific wheels for macOS (x86_64/arm64), Linux (x86_64/aarch64), and Windows; no BSD wheel is published on PyPI.
The rebar support matrix explicitly includes 'BSD' under 'Platform and venue'.

The plan's runtime fallback ('If the binary is unavailable or conversion raises, return the original Markdown unchanged') only executes after a successful install; it cannot rescue a pip install failure.
findings.finding: The plan pins `pypandoc-binary` (a pre-built binary wheel) as a hard project-metadata dependency. On BSD platforms — which are in the rebar support matrix — no pypandoc-binary wheel exists for that OS. When pip resolves the dependency on a BSD host it will either fail to find a compatible wheel and abort the install entirely (if no sdist fallback builds pandoc from source), or raise a ResolutionImpossible error, blocking environment setup before any runtime fallback logic can execute.
findings.location: Implementation section: 'Pin pypandoc-binary rather than system pypandoc so CI plus supported installs receive the binary from the wheel.'
scenarios: BSD developer workstation or BSD CI runner: `pip install rebar` (or equivalent) fails with 'No matching distribution found for pypandoc-binary' or a wheel-incompatibility error, preventing rebar from being installed at all — the runtime fallback never runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare pypandoc-binary as an optional dependency under an extras group (e.g. `[dc-wiki]`) and document that the renderer silently falls back to identity without it; or add a platform marker (`; sys_platform != 'freebsd'`) to the dependency declaration.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify and document which architectures pypandoc-binary ships a bundled pandoc binary for (x86-64, arm64) and add an explicit CI check or test-skip guard for the enrichment-floor test on architectures where the binary is not bundled.
evidence: PyPI pypandoc-binary page: 'Be aware that this works only on 64bit intel systems, as we only download it from the official releases.'
GitHub issue #355 on JessicaTegner/pypandoc: 'Is it possible to upgrade pypandoc_binary to directly support linux/arm64?' (Feb 2024)

Release notes: 'This release includes the new prebuild wheels for linux with pandoc included. We also now support a new variant of linux "aarch"' — aarch64 support added v1.13 (Feb 2024), but the PyPI page language above suggests it remains incomplete or conditionally built
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'CI plus supported installs receive the binary from the wheel' for pypandoc-binary, but the PyPI documentation for pypandoc-binary explicitly states that the prebuilt Linux wheel 'works only on 64bit intel systems, as we only download it from the official releases.' ARM-based Linux CI runners (e.g. GitHub Actions arm64, AWS Graviton) would not receive a bundled binary from the wheel and would silently fall back to the identity renderer, making the entire enrichment capability absent without any test failure.
findings.location: Implementation section — 'Pin pypandoc-binary rather than system pypandoc so CI plus supported installs receive the binary from the wheel'
scenarios: If the repo's CI or deployment targets run on Linux ARM64 (aarch64), the pypandoc-binary wheel may not include a bundled pandoc binary, causing silent fallback to identity rendering in exactly the environments the plan claims 'receive the binary from the wheel.'
A developer on an Apple Silicon Mac running a Linux ARM64 Docker container for CI parity would see fallback behavior without any warning.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the enrichment floor numerically in the AC (e.g., '≥68% of bodies and ≥78% of characters enriched') and define 'prose corruption' operationally (e.g., 'no prose word present in the input is absent from the output, verified by token-diff against the 249-fixture set').
evidence: Problem section states '68% of bodies / 78% of characters' but the AC says only 'recorded enrichment floor' with no forward reference to these numbers.
'Zero detected prose corruption' is not defined — no diff strategy, no comparison baseline, no mechanism.
findings.finding: The AC 'The vendored corpus meets the recorded enrichment floor with zero detected prose corruption' references a 'recorded enrichment floor' without stating the numeric value inline, and 'zero detected prose corruption' has no operational definition. An agent cannot write a passing assertion without knowing what number to assert and what check constitutes 'no corruption'.
findings.location: AC: 'The vendored corpus meets the recorded enrichment floor with zero detected prose corruption' / Tests section: 'corpus coverage calculation reaches the recorded enrichment floor'
scenarios: An agent writing the corpus test has no assertion value to hard-code or compare against.
Two reviewers cannot agree whether the AC passes because 'prose corruption' is undefined.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the AC as: 'The vendored corpus test asserts ≥68% of bodies and ≥78% of characters enriched; prose corruption is defined as zero input prose tokens dropped or altered in rendered output paragraphs, verified by comparing tokenized input vs. output for all non-bypassed blocks.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the availability-probe lifecycle (e.g., 'probe at module import using a module-level boolean; log the fallback at most once per process via a module-level flag') so probe timing and log deduplication are unambiguous.
evidence: 'Probe availability once' — timing unspecified.
'log the fallback once' — deduplication scope unspecified (per-process? per-module? per-call?).
findings.finding: The plan says 'Probe availability once' for pandoc but does not specify when 'once' occurs (module import time, first call, or a lazy singleton). The AC 'Missing pandoc returns the exact input plus logs the fallback once' uses a different sense of 'once' (log deduplication). These two different 'once' constraints interact: a call-time probe could log on every call unless separately deduplicated.
findings.location: Implementation section: 'Probe availability once. If the binary is unavailable or conversion raises, return the original Markdown unchanged plus log the fallback once.'
scenarios: An agent probing at call-time re-probes on every invocation unless they add a separate flag, which is a separate design decision the plan doesn't specify.
An agent probing at import time may cause import-time side effects incompatible with test isolation.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Implementation: 'Cache probe result at module load in a `_PANDOC_AVAILABLE` module-level bool. Log the fallback at most once per process using a `_FALLBACK_LOGGED` module-level flag set on first fallback.'

findings.finding: The plan asserts `pandoc -f commonmark -t jira --wrap=none` as the conversion command, but pandoc's `jira` output writer is NOT a standard writer in recent pandoc releases — it was removed from the bundled binary after being available only as a contrib writer in older versions. The specific pandoc version bundled by `pypandoc-binary` and whether it includes a working `-t jira` writer is unverified. If the bundled binary lacks this format, every render call immediately hits the fallback path and the feature is entirely inoperative.
findings.location: Implementation section: 'Send structurally safe headings, lists, fenced code, quotes, plus safe paragraphs through pandoc using -f commonmark -t jira --wrap=none'
scenarios: CI installs `pypandoc-binary`, pandoc binary launches, `pandoc --list-output-formats` does not include `jira`, every `convert_text(..., 'jira', ...)` raises PandocError, renderer silently falls back to identity on all bodies, and the entire feature ships with zero enrichment while all tests that mock the pandoc call still pass.
Developer installs on macOS with Homebrew pandoc (system binary), which also lacks `jira` writer, causing confusing discrepancy between local runs and CI.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `python -c "import pypandoc; print(pypandoc.get_pandoc_version()); print('jira' in pypandoc.get_pandoc_formats()[1])"` against the installed `pypandoc-binary` wheel to confirm. If the `jira` writer is absent, the plan must either (a) use a pandoc version that includes it (pypandoc-binary bundles pandoc 3.x where `jira` was re-added as a built-in writer in pandoc ≥3.0.1), or (b) replace `-t jira` with a hand-rolled Jira wiki renderer and drop the pandoc dependency for the output step entirely. Document the confirmed pandoc version floor in `pyproject.toml`.
